exposure: COVID-19 vaccination status (at least one dose vs. unvaccinated)
outcome: Use of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH)
Mode of birth (spontaneous vaginal delivery, instrumental delivery, emergency cesarean section, elective cesarean section)
cohort: A total of 164 pregnant women in Hong Kong, China, with a laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and a cycle threshold (Ct) value result available on admission to eight local hospitals.
finding: The overall rate of severe COVID-19 in pregnant women was low, and COVID-19 vaccination did not significantly impact maternal outcomes (except for increased LMWH use in vaccinated patients) or fetal outcomes and pregnancy complications.
mod_finding: The study reported that 56.10% of women had a spontaneous vaginal delivery, 4.27% had an instrumental delivery, 26.83% underwent emergency cesarean sections, and 12.80% had elective cesarean sections.
birth_weight: Four (2.65%) non-preterm babies had low birthweight, and the median birthweight percentile was 52.18th.
gest_age: COVID-19 was diagnosed before 28 weeks' gestation in 18.29% and at or after 28 weeks' gestation in 81.71% of women; 8.48% of babies were born preterm.
